repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
    wait until(not ((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true))
    triggered = false
}
wait until((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(100, 0)
delay(3 SEC)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(0, 0)
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The candidate uses a periodic `if` guard to detect the rising edge, but the IR requires a blocking wait that fires immediately when the condition becomes true. Evidence F2 shows the motion sensor turned true at 100ms, but the JoI emitted no action because the `if` guard only evaluates at the start of the 1000ms wrapper period. The fix replaces the periodic guard with the standard two-wait rearming pattern: wait for false, then block until true, then execute the body.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic `if` guard with a blocking rearming sequence (`wait until(not C)` then `wait until(C)`) to ensure the rising edge is caught immediately upon occurrence, matching the IR's `wait(..., edge rising)` semantics.
